definition_zh: 一个；某一个；任何一种；每一；某位；表示身份或职业；若干（数量结构）；固定短语中的虚指
definition_en: the indefinite article, used before a singular countable noun to mean one, any one, a certain one, or one per unit
core_image: 从一排东西里伸出一根手指点出一个，却不说明究竟是哪一个
scene: 清早的集市上，摊主随手拿起一个水果递给顾客。The vendor handed me a ripe peach and smiled.
sceneCN: 这里 a 是「一个」的不定冠词（第 1 个义项：首次提及的单个事物）；句意为摊主递给我一个熟桃，并笑了笑。

pos.zh: 冠词：不定冠词，表示一个、某一个或任何一种
限定词：用于数量结构与固定短语中的虚指

derivatives.zh: 由 a 在元音音素前分化出的变体，义为「一个」，与 a 是同一冠词的不同形式
与 a 同出古英语 ān 的数词，义为「一、一个」，属同源词而非派生词
由数词 one 加后缀构成，义为「一次；曾经」，与 a 共享同一词源

senses.title: One item mentioned for the first time
senses.definition: used before a singular countable noun when the thing is mentioned for the first time and is not yet known to the listener
senses.definitionCN: 用于单数可数名词前，指首次提到、听者尚不知晓的事物
senses.example: She bought a laptop yesterday.
senses.exampleCN: 她昨天买了一台笔记本电脑。
senses.why: The core image is one finger raised out of a group: a single, as yet unidentified item is picked out.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是从一群当中竖起的一根手指：点出一个单独但尚未确定的对象。

senses.title: Any one, not a particular one
senses.titleCN: 泛指任何一个（不确定的某一个）
senses.definition: used when the speaker means any one of a group but does not specify which member is intended
senses.definitionCN: 说话人指群体中的任何一个，但并不指明具体是哪一个成员
senses.example: I need a doctor, any doctor.
senses.exampleCN: 我需要一位医生，哪一位都行。
senses.why: The raised finger points at the class rather than at an individual member, so no particular item is fixed.
senses.whyCN: 竖起的手指指向整个类别而不是某个成员，因此没有锁定具体对象。

senses.title: A whole class represented by one member
senses.titleCN: 类指：用一个个例代表整个类别
senses.definition: used before a singular countable noun to make a general statement about the whole class
senses.definitionCN: 用于单数可数名词前，对整个类别作一般性陈述
senses.example: A dog is an animal.
senses.exampleCN: 狗是一种动物。
senses.why: One member stands in for all members: the single finger is shown as a sample of the whole hand.
senses.whyCN: 以一个成员代表全部成员：竖起的一根手指被当作整只手的样本。

senses.title: One per unit of time or amount
senses.definition: used before a singular noun to mean one for each unit of time, distance or amount
senses.definitionCN: 用于单数名词前，表示每一单位时间、距离或数量对应一个
senses.example: He earns fifty pounds a day.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天挣五十英镑。
senses.why: The single item is repeated for every unit: one finger counted again and again at each step.
senses.whyCN: 单个对象在每个单位上重复出现：每走一步就再数一次那根手指。

senses.title: A certain person unknown to the speaker
senses.titleCN: 某一位（说话人也不认识的）
senses.definition: used before a proper name to mean a certain person whom the speaker does not know well or does not identify
senses.definitionCN: 用于专有名词前，表示说话人不熟悉或不具体指明某位人士
senses.example: A Mr Brown called while you were out.
senses.exampleCN: 你不在时，有位布朗先生来过电话。
senses.why: The person is real but unnamed in the mind: one finger points, yet the face stays blank.
senses.whyCN: 这个人是真实的，但在心里没有名字：手指指出来了，面孔却仍是空白。

senses.title: Identity or profession after a linking verb
senses.definition: used before a singular noun after be or a similar verb to say what someone or something is
senses.definitionCN: 用于 be 等系动词之后的单数名词前，说明某人或某物是什么
senses.example: Her father is a teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 她父亲是一名教师。
senses.why: The item is classified rather than counted: the finger places it into a category.
senses.whyCN: 这里不是在计数，而是在归类：手指把对象放进一个类别。

senses.title: Part of a quantity expression
senses.titleCN: 用于数量结构中的冠词
senses.definition: used in fixed quantity expressions such as a few, a little and a great many
senses.definitionCN: 用于 a few、a little、a great many 等固定的数量表达中
senses.example: Only a few seats were left.
senses.exampleCN: 只剩下几个座位。
senses.why: Here the article has lost its counting force and simply forms part of a fixed quantity phrase.
senses.whyCN: 这里的冠词已经没有计数作用，只是构成固定数量短语的一部分。

senses.title: The vague article in fixed phrases
senses.definition: used in idioms such as at a loss and in a hurry, where it no longer points to a specific item
senses.definitionCN: 用于 at a loss、in a hurry 等习语，此时它已不指某个具体事物
senses.example: The sudden question left him at a loss.
senses.exampleCN: 这个突然的问题让他不知所措。
senses.why: The finger still appears, but it points at nothing in particular: the phrase has frozen the article into an idiom.
senses.whyCN: 手指还在，却不再指任何具体事物：短语已经把冠词凝固成习语。

intro.en: A is the Old English numeral ān weakened in unstressed positions; it shares its origin with one and has no direct Latin cognate.
intro.cn: a 是古英语数词 ān「一」在非重读位置弱化而来的冠词，与 one 同源；它没有直接来自拉丁语的同族词。

items.en: *oinos or *oi-no- is generally reconstructed as 'one, single'; the exact shape and deeper origin are source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *oinos 或 *oi-no- 表示「一、单个」；确切形式与更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old English ān meant 'one, alone, single' and was the common ancestor of both an and one.
items.cn: 古英语 ān 意为「一、独自、单个」，是 an 与 one 的共同祖先。

items.en: In unstressed positions the numeral weakened to a before consonants and to an before vowels; the change was gradual and its dating is uncertain.
items.cn: 在非重读位置，这个数词在辅音前弱化为 a，在元音前作 an；变化是渐进的，具体年代不确定。

items.en: Printing helped fix the modern distribution of a and an, though older texts vary.
items.cn: 印刷术帮助固定了 a 与 an 的现代分工，更早的文本则并不统一。

items.en: The form became a purely grammatical word, keeping the idea of oneness while adding generic, per-unit and idiomatic uses.
items.cn: 这个形式成为纯粹的语法词，保留「一」的观念，又发展出类指、每单位与习语用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the article's own forms and the numeral it came from; the near-meaning group collects other determiners that also point at quantity or identity.
note.cn: 形近组收冠词自身的形式与它来源的数词；近义组收其他同样表示数量或指认的限定词。

entries.definition: The form of the indefinite article used before a word beginning with a vowel sound.
entries.definitionCN: 不定冠词在元音音素开头词前的形式，义为「一个」。

entries.definition: The numeral for the number 1, from the same Old English ān as the article.
entries.definitionCN: 数词，义为「一」，与冠词 a 同出古英语 ān。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning one time; it is built on the same numeral as one.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「一次；曾经」，由与 one 相同的数词构成。

entries.definition: A determiner meaning whichever one or some; its history is separate, and it only looks and sounds close.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，义为「任何一个」，历史来源不同，只是拼写与读音相近。

entries.definition: The definite article, used for an item already known to both speaker and listener.
entries.definitionCN: 定冠词，用于说话双方都已知晓的对象，与不定冠词 a 相对。

entries.definition: A determiner for an unspecified amount or number, often the plural counterpart of a.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，表示不确定的数量，常与 a 构成单复数对照。

entries.definition: A determiner meaning every one taken separately.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，义为「每一个」，强调逐个看待。

entries.definition: A preposition meaning for each unit, close to the per-unit sense of a.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「每」，与 a 的每单位用法接近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English numeral and the fixed phrases the article actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语数词，以及冠词实际出现的固定短语。

normal.en: Old English ān 'one' is the shared ancestor of a, an and one.
normal.cn: 古英语 ān「一」是 a、an 与 one 的共同祖先。

normal.en: Before a vowel sound the same article is written an.
normal.cn: 在元音音素之前，同一个冠词写作 an。

normal.en: A few, a little and a great many keep the article inside fixed quantity phrases.
normal.cn: 在「a few」「a little」「a great many」这些固定数量短语里，冠词被保留下来。

normal.en: Twice a week shows the per-unit pattern of one for each period.
normal.cn: 「twice a week」展示了每单位一个的模式：每个周期一个。

normal.en: At a loss and in a hurry show the article frozen inside idioms.
normal.cn: 「at a loss」与「in a hurry」展示了冠词被凝固在习语中的用法。

abstract.en: Picture a hand rising from a crowd with one finger up: it picks out one thing, but its face is still unknown.
abstract.cn: 想象人群中举起一只手，只伸出一根手指：它点出一个东西，但那东西的面貌仍然未知。

abstract.en: The same finger points at a whole class when it stands for every member, as in the sentence about a dog.
abstract.cn: 当它代表全体成员时，同一根手指指向整个类别，就像那句关于狗的话。

abstract.en: In idioms the finger still points, but at nothing in particular, which is why the article feels almost empty.
abstract.cn: 在习语里手指仍在指，却不指任何具体事物，所以这个冠词显得几乎是空的。

examples.en: A cat sat on the warm roof.
examples.cn: 一只猫坐在温暖的屋顶上。

examples.en: She is a nurse at the city hospital.
examples.cn: 她是市医院的一名护士。

examples.en: The old map was drawn a century ago.
examples.cn: 那张旧地图是一个世纪前绘制的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呃」——张口轻轻一声，点出一个东西：一个

root: 古英语 ān「一」在非重读位置弱化为 a（元音音素前作 an），与 one 同源；更早可上溯到印欧语数词 *oi-no-，拉丁语中没有直接对应的同族冠词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight uses of a all start from one raised finger: first mention, unspecified choice, a whole class, one per unit, an unknown person, an identity, a quantity phrase, and a frozen idiom.
sensesIntro.cn: a 的八种用法都从竖起的一根手指出发：首次提及、不特定选择、整个类别、每单位一个、不认识的某位、身份归类、数量短语，以及凝固的习语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one finger is raised out of a group, pointing at a single item whose identity stays open.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一群当中竖起一根手指，点出一个单独的对象，其身份仍然开放。

branches.en: FIRST MENTION: the item is new to the listener, so the finger simply marks one thing.
branches.cn: 首次提及线：对象对听者是新的，手指只是标出一个东西。

branches.en: CHOICE AND CLASS: the finger may point at any member or at the class through one member.
branches.cn: 选择与类别线：手指可以指向任一成员，也可以借一个成员指向整个类别。

branches.en: PER UNIT: the single item is counted again for every period or measure.
branches.cn: 每单位线：单个对象在每个周期或度量上反复计数。

branches.en: IDENTITY: the same article introduces an unknown person or names what someone is.
branches.cn: 身份线：同一个冠词可以引出不认识的人，也可以说明某人的身份。

branches.en: FIXED PATTERNS: quantity phrases and idioms freeze the article into set expressions.
branches.cn: 固定模式线：数量短语与习语把冠词凝固成固定表达。

intro.en: A is not built with prefixes; this section gathers the article's own forms and the numeral root behind them.
intro.cn: a 并非由前缀构成；这一部分收的是冠词自身的形式，以及它背后的数词词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no matching indefinite article, and no direct Latin cognate of the English article is recorded, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语没有对应的不定冠词，也没有记录到与英语冠词直接同源的拉丁词，因此拉丁同族一栏留空。

definition_zh: 意外的；偶然的；非本质的；（音乐）临时记号的
definition_en: happening by chance and without intention, or belonging to a thing only as a non-essential property
core_image: 低头走路时，一颗石子从侧面飞来，正好落在脚前
scene: 雨后的石板路很滑，行人小心地绕过一摊水洼。His fall was accidental, caused by a loose stone on the path.
sceneCN: 这里 accidental 是「意外的、非故意的」（第 1 个义项：不是有意造成的）；句意为他的摔倒是由路上松动的石块造成的意外。

pos.zh: 形容词：意外的、偶然的；非本质的
名词：（音乐）临时记号；非本质属性

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「偶然地；意外地」
由拉丁动词 accidere 的名词形式构成，义为「事故；意外」，是本词的词根词
由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「偶然性」，极少使用
由 accident 与 prone 复合而成，义为「易出事故的」

senses.title: Done without intention
senses.definition: done or caused without intending to do it, when the result was never part of the plan
senses.definitionCN: 做或造成某事时并无此意，结果从不在计划之内
senses.example: The mistake was accidental; she did not mean to delete the file.
senses.exampleCN: 这个错误是偶然的，她并非有意删除文件。
senses.why: The core image is a stone arriving from outside: what happens was never part of the plan.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是从外面飞来的石子：发生的事从来不在计划之中。

senses.title: Happening by chance
senses.definition: occurring through chance rather than through a planned or expected cause
senses.definitionCN: 因偶然而非计划或预期的原因而发生
senses.example: Their accidental meeting at the station led to a long friendship.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在车站的偶然相遇促成了一段长久的友谊。
senses.why: An event, not only an act, can fall on someone; chance replaces intention as the cause.
senses.whyCN: 不只是行为，事件也可以「落到」某人身上；偶然取代意图成为原因。

senses.title: A non-essential property
senses.definition: in philosophy, a property that a thing may have or lose without ceasing to be what it is
senses.definitionCN: 哲学上指某物可以拥有或失去、却不因此改变其本质的属性
senses.example: Being red is an accidental property of the cup, not part of its essence.
senses.exampleCN: 红色是这只杯子的偶性，并不属于它的本质。
senses.why: What falls onto a thing stays outside its essence, like dust settling on a table.
senses.whyCN: 落到事物身上的东西留在其本质之外，就像落在桌面上的灰尘。

senses.title: Accidental damage in insurance
senses.definition: damage to property caused by an unexpected event rather than by wear or deliberate action
senses.definitionCN: 由意外事件而非自然损耗或故意行为造成的财产损坏
senses.example: The policy covers accidental damage to the laptop screen.
senses.exampleCN: 这份保险承保笔记本电脑屏幕的意外损坏。
senses.why: Insurance names the outside event that falls on property; the falling stone becomes a category of risk.
senses.whyCN: 保险为落到财产上的外部事件命名；那颗落下的石子成了风险类别。

senses.title: Accidental death in law
senses.definition: a death caused by an unintended external event, treated as a legal and insurance category
senses.definitionCN: 由非故意的外部事件造成的死亡，作为法律与保险上的类别处理
senses.example: The court recorded the death as accidental.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭将这场死亡记为意外死亡。
senses.why: Law fixes chance as a cause and turns the falling event into a legal category.
senses.whyCN: 法律把偶然固定为一种原因，把「落下的事件」变成法律类别。

senses.title: Accidental release in technology
senses.definition: the unintended escape of a substance, gas or data from a controlled system
senses.definitionCN: 物质、气体或数据从受控系统中非故意地逸出
senses.example: The accidental release of chlorine forced the plant to close.
senses.exampleCN: 氯气的意外泄漏迫使工厂停产。
senses.why: Something escapes the boundary meant to hold it; the falling stone is now a leak.
senses.whyCN: 某物冲出了本该拦住它的边界；那颗落下的石子在这里变成了一次泄漏。

senses.title: A chance coincidence
senses.definition: a coincidence that appears meaningful but arises purely from chance
senses.definitionCN: 看起来有意义、实际却完全出于偶然的巧合
senses.example: It was an accidental coincidence that both chose the same train.
senses.exampleCN: 两人选了同一班列车，纯属偶然的巧合。
senses.why: Two paths cross without plan, as if stones from different directions met at one point.
senses.whyCN: 两条路径未经计划地交叉，就像来自不同方向的石子在一点相遇。

senses.title: A temporary sign in music
senses.definition: a sign that raises or lowers a note for one passage without changing the key
senses.definitionCN: 在一段乐句中升高或降低某音符、却不改变调性的记号
senses.example: The accidental on the third line lasts only to the end of the bar.
senses.exampleCN: 第三行的临时记号只持续到本小节结束。
senses.why: The sign is added from outside the key and falls away again, just as an external event touches a thing briefly.
senses.whyCN: 记号从调性之外加入，随后又消失，正如外部事件短暂地触碰某物。

intro.en: Accidental is built on accident, whose Latin source describes something falling onto a person.
intro.cn: accidental 由 accident 加后缀构成，其拉丁来源描述的是「落到某人身上」的事。

items.en: *kad- 'to fall' is generally reconstructed for the family; the deeper origin of the root is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为这一词族来自原始印欧语 *kad-「落下」；这一词根更早的来源不确定。

items.en: cadere meant 'to fall'; with the prefix ad- it formed accidere, 'to fall to, happen, befall'.
items.cn: cadere 意为「落下」；加上前缀 ad- 构成 accidere，义为「落到、发生、降临」。

items.en: The participle accidens named what befalls a thing without belonging to its essence, and Late Latin accidentalis was formed on the same stem.
items.cn: 分词 accidens 指降临到某物、却不属于其本质的东西；晚期拉丁语又在同一词干上构成 accidentalis。

items.en: Old French accident and accidentel carried the noun and the adjective into English; the exact borrowing dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 古法语 accident 与 accidentel 把名词和形容词带入英语；确切的借入年代不确定。

items.en: Insurance, law and music each fixed a technical sense, from accidental damage to the accidental in a score.
items.cn: 保险、法律与音乐各自固定了专门义项，从「意外损坏」一直到乐谱上的「临时记号」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same Latin verb for falling; the near-meaning group gathers words for what happens without design.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁动词「落下」构成的词；近义组收表示「非计划而发生」的词。

entries.definition: A noun for an unexpected event that causes damage or injury, built on the same falling verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事故、意外」，指造成损害或伤害的意外事件，与 accidental 同出「落下」词根。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning by chance or without intention.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「偶然地、意外地」，由本词加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning happening as a minor part of something else, from in- plus cadere.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「附带的、次要的」，由 in- 加 cadere「落下」构成，与 accidental 同根。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning happening at the same time by chance, from co- plus incidere.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「同时发生而巧合的」，由 co- 加 incidere 构成，同属 cadere 词根。

entries.definition: A noun for a person killed or injured in an event; its stem also goes back to casus, a fall.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伤亡人员」，其词干也可上溯到 casus「落下」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: Adjective meaning not done on purpose, with the focus on the missing intention rather than on chance.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「非故意的」，侧重「没有意图」，而不是强调偶然。

entries.definition: An adjective or noun for something that happens without a planned cause.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「偶然的、机会」，指没有计划原因而发生。

entries.definition: Adjective meaning chosen or occurring without any pattern or plan.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「随机的、无规律的」，强调没有模式或计划。

entries.definition: A formal adjective meaning happening by luck, often with a fortunate result.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，形容词，义为「偶然发生的」，常含「运气好」的意味。

entries.definition: Adjective meaning informal, unplanned or done without serious intent.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「随便的、非正式的」，也可指没有认真打算。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb for falling and the technical phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「落下」动词，以及这个词实际出现的专门搭配。

normal.en: cadere is to fall: something accidental falls onto us from outside the plan.
normal.cn: cadere 是「落下」：意外之事是从计划之外落到我们身上的。

normal.en: ad- plus cadere gives accidere, to happen or befall.
normal.cn: ad- 加 cadere 得到 accidere，义为「发生、降临」。

normal.en: The participle accidens gives the philosophical sense of a non-essential property.
normal.cn: 分词 accidens 给出了哲学上「偶性、非本质属性」的义项。

normal.en: accidentally is the everyday adverb made with -ly.
normal.cn: accidentally 是加 -ly 构成的日常副词。

normal.en: Insurance speaks of accidental damage, law of accidental death, and music of an accidental.
normal.cn: 保险说「accidental damage」，法律说「accidental death」，音乐则说「an accidental」。

abstract.en: Picture a stone rolling off a cliff and landing beside a walker: nothing about it was arranged.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗石子从崖边滚落，正好落在行人脚边：没有任何一环是安排好的。

abstract.en: The same stone can be a legal category, an insurance clause or a musical sign: each names what came from outside.
abstract.cn: 同一颗石子可以成为法律类别、保险条款或音乐记号：它们都在命名来自外部的东西。

abstract.en: The sign on a score is added and then forgotten, like dust that settles and is brushed away.
abstract.cn: 乐谱上的记号被加上又被遗忘，就像落下的灰尘被轻轻拂去。

examples.en: The fire was accidental, started by a faulty wire.
examples.cn: 这场火是意外燃起的，起因是一根故障电线。

examples.en: Their meeting was purely accidental.
examples.cn: 他们的相遇纯属偶然。

examples.en: Accidental damage is covered by this policy.
examples.cn: 本保险承保意外损坏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克西登特」——石子从路边飞来，正好落在脚前：意外

root: 拉丁语 accidere（ad-「向」+ cadere「落下」）意为「落到、发生」；分词 accidens 指不属于本质、偶然附上的性质，accidental 即「意外降临的、非本质的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of accidental all come from something falling onto a scene from outside: an unintended act, a chance event, a non-essential property, and technical uses in insurance, law, technology, music and coincidence.
sensesIntro.cn: accidental 的八个义项都来自「从外部落到现场」的东西：非故意的行为、偶然事件、非本质属性，以及保险、法律、技术、音乐与巧合中的专门用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone rolls in from the side and lands beside a walker, outside every plan.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗石子从侧面滚来，落在行人脚边，完全在计划之外。

branches.en: INTENTION AND CHANCE: the stone may describe an act nobody meant or an event nobody planned.
branches.cn: 意图与偶然线：石子既可以指没人有意做的行为，也可以指没人计划的事件。

branches.en: ESSENCE: what falls onto a thing stays outside its essence, which gives the philosophical sense.
branches.cn: 本质线：落到事物上的东西留在本质之外，这就产生哲学上的偶性义。

branches.en: RISK AND LAW: insurance, law and technology name the outside event as damage, death or a release.
branches.cn: 风险与法律线：保险、法律与技术把外部事件命名为损坏、死亡或泄漏。

branches.en: COINCIDENCE: two unplanned paths cross at one point and look meaningful.
branches.cn: 巧合一词线：两条未计划的路径在某点交叉，显得意味深长。

branches.en: NOTATION: the musical sign is added from outside the key and then removed.
branches.cn: 记号线：音乐记号从调性之外加入，随后又被撤去。

intro.en: Accidental is a Latin verb stem plus a Latin prefix, with English suffixes building the rest of the family.
intro.cn: accidental 由拉丁动词词干与拉丁前缀构成，英语再用后缀扩展出整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin cadere, accidere, accidens and accidentalis are all recorded, so only the Indo-European root behind them is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cadere、accidere、accidens 与 accidentalis 均有文献记录，只有它们背后的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.exampleCN: 它把 cadere 变成 accidere。

items.example: The verb is the falling root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是词族的「落下」词根。
这个复合词给出了英语 accident。
它提供了哲学上的义项。

items.example: The noun is the base of accidental.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是 accidental 的基础。
它由 accident 构成 accidental。
它构成 accidentally。
它构成 accidentalness。

definition_zh: 使习惯；使适应；使熟悉；使耐受
definition_en: to make someone or oneself familiar with something through repeated experience until it feels usual
core_image: 新鞋穿了一整个夏天，脚形慢慢被磨合成鞋的样子，走路不再觉得硌
scene: 海边的孩子每天迎着风走路上学。Years of walking to school had accustomed him to the cold salt wind.
sceneCN: 这里 accustom 是「使习惯」（第 1 个义项：使某人逐渐习惯某事）；句意为多年步行上学使他习惯了寒冷的海风。

pos.zh: 动词：使习惯；使适应；使熟悉

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「习惯的；惯常的」
由本词加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不习惯的；不适应的」
由 accustomed 加 -ness 构成名词，义为「习惯状态」，极少使用

senses.title: To make someone used to something
senses.definition: to make a person gradually familiar with a situation, so that it no longer feels new or strange
senses.definitionCN: 使某人逐渐熟悉某种处境，使之不再显得新鲜或陌生
senses.example: The coach accustomed the young players to early training.
senses.exampleCN: 教练让年轻球员习惯了清早训练。
senses.why: Repeated contact wears down surprise, like a new shoe softened by walking.
senses.whyCN: 反复接触磨掉了陌生感，就像新鞋被走路磨合。

senses.title: To acclimatize to a place or climate
senses.definition: to make a person or body able to live comfortably in a new climate or surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或身体能在新的气候或环境中舒适地生活
senses.example: It took a month to accustom the team to the high altitude.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍花了一个月才适应高海拔。
senses.why: The body adjusts to thin air step by step, by the same repeated exposure.
senses.whyCN: 身体靠着同样的反复接触，一步步适应稀薄的空气。

senses.title: To familiarize with a procedure
senses.definition: to make someone familiar with a method, tool or routine through repeated practice
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复练习使某人熟悉某种方法、工具或流程
senses.example: Nurses accustom new staff to the hospital record system.
senses.exampleCN: 护士们让新员工熟悉医院的病历系统。
senses.why: A routine is learned by repeating it until the steps come without thinking.
senses.whyCN: 流程是靠反复做来学会的，直到每个步骤都不用想就能完成。

senses.title: To train a response automatically
senses.definition: to train a person or animal to respond to a signal automatically through repetition
senses.definitionCN: 通过重复训练使人或动物对某个信号自动作出反应
senses.example: The handler accustomed the dog to the sound of the whistle.
senses.exampleCN: 驯养员让那只狗习惯了哨声。
senses.why: The same signal returns again and again until the response becomes automatic.
senses.whyCN: 同一个信号反复出现，直到反应变得自动。

senses.title: To inure the body to hardship
senses.definition: to make the body able to endure hardship, pain or a harmful substance without much reaction
senses.definitionCN: 使身体能承受艰苦、疼痛或有害物质而反应不大
senses.example: Cold baths accustomed the swimmers to low temperatures.
senses.exampleCN: 冷水浴使游泳者耐受低温。
senses.why: Endurance grows as the body meets the same hardship repeatedly.
senses.whyCN: 身体反复面对同一种艰苦，忍耐力便随之增长。

senses.title: Be accustomed to: already used to
senses.titleCN: be accustomed to 表示已经习惯
senses.definition: in the pattern be accustomed to, to be in the settled state of being used to something
senses.definitionCN: 用于 be accustomed to 结构，表示已处于习惯某事的状态
senses.example: The villagers are accustomed to long dry summers.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们已经习惯了漫长的干旱夏季。
senses.why: The participle names a settled state, not a process still going on.
senses.whyCN: 分词形式命名的是一种已经稳定的状态，而不是仍在进行的过程。

senses.title: Accustom oneself: self-adjustment
senses.definition: in the reflexive pattern accustom oneself to, to make oneself gradually used to something
senses.definitionCN: 用于反身结构 accustom oneself to，表示使自己逐渐习惯某事
senses.example: She accustomed herself to working night shifts.
senses.exampleCN: 她使自己习惯了上夜班。
senses.why: The one who adjusts and the one adjusted are the same person.
senses.whyCN: 做出调整的人与被调整的人，在这里是同一个人。

senses.title: To make customary in older usage
senses.definition: in older usage, to make something customary or to establish a practice by habit
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的用法，指使某事成为惯例，或以习惯确立某种做法
senses.example: The old guild accustomed its members to a fixed scale of fees.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的行会使其成员习惯于固定的收费等级。
senses.why: If repetition makes a habit, then the word once also meant making a practice standard.
senses.whyCN: 如果重复能造出习惯，那么这个词曾经也指把某种做法确立为标准。

intro.en: Accustom came from Old French, and its root is the Latin word for custom or habit.
intro.cn: accustom 来自古法语，其词根是拉丁语中表示「习俗、习惯」的词。

items.en: consuetudo meant 'custom, habit'; it came from consuescere 'to become used', built on con- and suescere.
items.cn: consuetudo 意为「习俗、习惯」，来自 consuescere「变得习惯」，后者由 con- 与 suescere 构成。

items.en: Old French costume meant 'custom, habitual practice', not a garment as in modern English.
items.cn: 古法语 costume 意为「习俗、惯常做法」，并非现代英语里的「服装」。

items.en: The prefix a- plus costume formed acostumer, 'to make accustomed, bring into a habit'.
items.cn: 前缀 a- 加 costume 构成 acostumer，义为「使习惯、使养成某种惯常做法」。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain and spellings vary.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个动词；确切首见年代不确定，早期拼写也不统一。

items.en: The participle accustomed outgrew the verb, and accustom now survives mainly in the reflexive and in formal prose.
items.cn: 分词形式 accustomed 的使用超过了动词本身，accustom 如今主要见于反身结构与正式书面语。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same custom root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of becoming used to something.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「习俗」词根构成的词；近义组收表示「逐渐习惯」的动词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning used to something, formed from the verb with -ed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「习惯的」，由动词加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: The negated adjective meaning not used to something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不习惯的」，由 accustomed 加否定前缀 un- 构成。

entries.definition: A noun for a habitual practice, from the same Latin consuetudo.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「习俗、惯例」，与 accustom 同出拉丁语 consuetudo。

entries.definition: A noun for clothing worn for a role; it comes from the same Old French word for custom, though the modern meaning changed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「戏服、服装」，来自同一个表示「习俗」的古法语词，但现代词义已经转移。

entries.definition: A formal verb meaning to make someone used to something by repetition.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，动词，义为「使习惯于」，强调反复接触。

entries.definition: To make someone learn about or become comfortable with something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使熟悉」，侧重让人了解某事物。

entries.definition: To adjust to a new climate or environment.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使适应气候或环境」，侧重自然环境。

entries.definition: A formal verb meaning to make someone endure something difficult without being affected.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，动词，义为「使惯于、使耐受」，侧重对艰苦的承受。

entries.definition: To train a person or animal to behave in a particular way.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「训练、使形成条件反射」，侧重行为塑造。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root for custom and the patterns the verb actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁「习俗」词根，以及动词实际出现的结构。

normal.en: consuetudo is custom: to accustom is to turn an experience into a custom.
normal.cn: consuetudo 是「习俗」：使习惯就是把一段经历变成习俗。

normal.en: costume once meant custom, so accustom and custom share a root.
normal.cn: costume 曾经意为「习俗」，所以 accustom 与 custom 共有一个词根。

normal.en: accustomed is the -ed adjective that now outnumbers the verb.
normal.cn: accustomed 是加 -ed 的形容词，如今出现次数远超动词本身。

normal.en: be accustomed to and become accustomed to both describe a settled state.
normal.cn: 「be accustomed to」与「become accustomed to」都描述一种已经稳定的状态。

normal.en: accustom oneself puts the changer and the changed in one person.
normal.cn: 「accustom oneself」把改变者与被改变者合在同一个人身上。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of new shoes worn every day until the leather takes the shape of the foot.
abstract.cn: 想象一双新鞋每天穿着，直到皮革慢慢贴合脚的形状。

abstract.en: The same routine repeated at dawn stops feeling strange, as if the path had always been there.
abstract.cn: 同一条路线在黎明反复走过，就不再觉得陌生，仿佛它一直都在。

abstract.en: Habit is not one big decision but many small returns to the same thing.
abstract.cn: 习惯不是一次大决定，而是许多次回到同一件事上。

examples.en: It took months to accustom the new staff to the night shift.
examples.cn: 让新员工习惯夜班花了几个月。

examples.en: She had accustomed herself to the noise of the machines.
examples.cn: 她已经使自己习惯了机器的噪音。

examples.en: The horses were accustomed to the sound of gunfire.
examples.cn: 那些马已经习惯了枪炮声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿卡斯特姆」——阿卡把一双鞋穿旧，脚也就习惯了

root: 古法语 acostumer 由 a- 加 costume「习俗」构成，costume 出自拉丁 consuetudo「习惯」；同族有 custom 与 accustomed。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of accustom follow one pattern: repeated contact turns something unfamiliar into a settled part of life, whether it is a place, a procedure, a signal, hardship, or a practice.
sensesIntro.cn: accustom 的八个义项都遵循同一模式：反复接触把陌生之物变成生活中稳定的一部分，无论那是地方、流程、信号、艰苦，还是一种做法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a new shoe is worn day after day until it takes the exact shape of the foot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双新鞋日复一日地穿，直到它完全贴合脚的形状。

branches.en: THE PROCESS AND THE STATE: repetition makes someone used to something, and the participle names the settled result.
branches.cn: 过程与状态线：重复使人习惯某事，分词形式则命名稳定的结果。

branches.en: THE ENVIRONMENT: a climate or altitude is met repeatedly until the body fits it.
branches.cn: 环境线：气候或海拔被反复接触，直到身体与之相合。

branches.en: THE ROUTINE: practice makes a procedure familiar, and a signal can train an automatic response.
branches.cn: 流程线：练习使流程变熟，而信号可以训练出自动反应。

branches.en: THE BODY: the same hardship met again and again builds endurance.
branches.cn: 身体线：同一种艰苦反复相遇，便积累出忍耐力。

branches.en: THE SELF AND THE NORM: one can accustom oneself, and older usage made a practice into a custom.
branches.cn: 自我与规范线：人可以自我适应，较旧的用法则把某种做法确立为惯例。

intro.en: Accustom is a French prefix and a French stem that goes back to Latin words for custom.
intro.cn: accustom 由一个法语前缀与一个法语词干构成，词干可上溯到拉丁语中表示「习俗」的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin consuetudo, consuescere and suescere are recorded, and assuetus is a related adjective, so only the oldest layer is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 consuetudo、consuescere 与 suescere 均有记录，assuetus 是相关的形容词，只有最古老的一层属于重构。

definition_zh: 疼痛；隐痛；渴望
definition_en: a continuous dull pain in part of the body, or to feel such pain, or to long for something strongly
core_image: 阴天里膝盖深处一阵一阵的钝痛，像有根细线一直在拉
scene: 雨前的旧屋里，老人扶着膝盖慢慢坐下。His knee began to ache as the rain came closer.
sceneCN: 这里 ache 是「隐隐作痛」（第 1 个义项：持续性的钝痛）；句意为雨意渐近时他的膝盖开始作痛。

pos.zh: 名词：疼痛；隐痛；渴望
动词：疼痛；渴望

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「疼痛的；酸痛的」
由 aching 加 -ly 构成，义为「极其；令人心痛地」
由 head 与 ache 复合而成，义为「头痛」
由 tooth 与 ache 复合而成，义为「牙痛」

senses.title: A continuous dull bodily pain
senses.definition: an ongoing, dull pain that is felt rather than sharply localized
senses.definitionCN: 一种持续存在、闷闷的疼痛，而不是尖锐的局部刺痛
senses.example: A dull ache spread across his shoulders by evening.
senses.exampleCN: 到傍晚时，一阵钝痛蔓延在他的双肩。
senses.why: The core image is a thin thread pulled steadily: the sensation is long and low rather than sudden.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一根被持续拉扯的细线：感觉绵长而低沉，而不是突然爆发。

senses.title: Pain in a particular body part
senses.definition: a pain located in one part of the body, such as a knee, back or ear
senses.definitionCN: 位于身体某个部位的疼痛，如膝盖、背部或耳朵
senses.example: The ache in her wrist kept her awake.
senses.exampleCN: 手腕的疼痛让她睡不着。
senses.why: The thread is tied to one spot, so the whole attention gathers there.
senses.whyCN: 细线被系在某一处，于是全部注意力都聚到那里。

senses.title: Emotional pain or heartache
senses.definition: a feeling of deep sadness or distress that is experienced almost like physical pain
senses.definitionCN: 一种几乎像身体疼痛一样的深切悲伤或痛苦
senses.example: There was an ache in her chest when she heard the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到那个消息时，她胸口一阵难受。
senses.why: The body's dull pain is borrowed for grief, because sorrow also feels like something pulling inside.
senses.whyCN: 身体的钝痛被借来形容悲伤，因为哀伤也像体内有什么在拉扯。

senses.title: To long for something strongly
senses.definition: in ache for or ache to do, to want something very strongly, often with sadness
senses.definitionCN: 用于 ache for 或 ache to do，表示强烈地想要某事，常带伤感
senses.example: She ached for a quiet room of her own.
senses.exampleCN: 她渴望有一间属于自己的安静房间。
senses.why: Longing is a pull that never stops, which is the same steady tension as a dull ache.
senses.whyCN: 渴望是一种停不下来的拉扯，与钝痛那种持续的紧绷是同一种感觉。

senses.title: To cause pain in older usage
senses.definition: in older texts, a transitive use meaning to cause someone pain or distress
senses.definitionCN: 在较旧的文本中作及物动词，义为使人疼痛或痛苦
senses.example: The wound ached him through the night.
senses.exampleCN: 那处伤口让他整夜疼痛。
senses.why: The same sensation is viewed from the other side: instead of feeling it, one makes another feel it.
senses.whyCN: 同一种感觉从另一面来看：不是自己感到痛，而是使别人感到痛。

senses.title: Muscle soreness after exertion
senses.definition: the stiffness and soreness in muscles that follows unusually hard exercise
senses.definitionCN: 异常剧烈的运动之后肌肉出现的僵硬与酸痛
senses.example: His legs ached for two days after the race.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛后他的双腿酸痛了两天。
senses.why: Effort leaves the muscle in a low, lasting tension, the same dull pull felt from inside.
senses.whyCN: 用力之后肌肉留下低而持久的紧绷，正是从内部感到的那种闷闷的拉扯。

senses.title: Pain fixed inside compound words
senses.titleCN: 构成复合词的痛（牙痛、头痛）
senses.definition: the second element in compounds such as toothache and headache, naming a specific kind of pain
senses.definitionCN: 在 toothache、headache 等复合词中作第二成分，指某一类疼痛
senses.example: A sudden toothache ruined his dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 突如其来的牙痛毁了他这顿晚饭。
senses.why: The general sensation is nailed to one named place, and the compound turns it into a specific ailment.
senses.whyCN: 笼统的感觉被钉在一个具体的部位名称上，复合词便把它变成一种具体的病痛。

senses.title: A lingering pain that outlasts its cause
senses.definition: a pain that continues after the injury or cause has passed, often for days
senses.definitionCN: 在受伤或原因过去之后仍然持续的疼痛，往往延续数日
senses.example: The ache lingered long after the bruise had faded.
senses.exampleCN: 淤青消退很久之后，那阵痛仍没有散。
senses.why: The thread keeps pulling even after the hand that pulled it is gone, which is the afterpain.
senses.whyCN: 即使拉线的手已经松开，细线仍在拉，这就是余痛。

intro.en: Ache is an Old English word, and its spelling was later reshaped in medical writing.
intro.cn: ache 是一个古英语词，其拼写在后来的医学写作中被重新塑造。

items.en: *aeg- 'pain, sickness' is generally reconstructed; the deeper origin of the root is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *aeg- 表示「疼痛、疾病」；这一词根更早的来源不确定。

items.en: The verb acan meant 'to ache, suffer pain' and the related noun was æce.
items.cn: 动词 acan 意为「疼痛、受苦」，相关的名词是 æce。

items.en: Forms such as ake and ache competed, and the pronunciation stayed the same through the change.
items.cn: ake 与 ache 等拼写曾经并存，变化过程中读音保持不变。

items.en: Medical writers respelled ache after Greek akhos 'pain'; the influence is generally accepted, though the detail is uncertain.
items.cn: 医学写作者参照希腊语 akhos「疼痛」改写拼写；这种影响一般认为成立，但细节不确定。

items.en: Compounds such as headache and toothache, and the figurative ache for, carried the word far beyond physical pain.
items.cn: headache、toothache 等复合词，以及比喻用法的 ache for，把这个词带到了身体疼痛之外。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derived and compound forms of the same word; the near-meaning group gathers different kinds of pain.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个词的派生形式与复合形式；近义组收不同种类的疼痛。

entries.definition: The -ing form used as an adjective for something that hurts dully.
entries.definitionCN: 加 -ing 的形式，作形容词表示「酸痛的、隐隐作痛的」。

entries.definition: A compound noun for a pain in the head.
entries.definitionCN: 复合名词，义为「头痛」，由 head 与 ache 构成。

entries.definition: A compound noun for a pain in a tooth or the teeth.
entries.definitionCN: 复合名词，义为「牙痛」，由 tooth 与 ache 构成。

entries.definition: A compound noun for a pain in the back.
entries.definitionCN: 复合名词，义为「背痛」，由 back 与 ache 构成。

entries.definition: The general word for physical suffering, stronger and broader than ache.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「疼痛」，是最一般的说法，语气比 ache 更强、范围更广。

entries.definition: The state of being tender and painful to touch, often after exercise.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「酸痛、压痛」，指一碰就疼的状态，常见于运动之后。

entries.definition: A short, sharp pain that comes suddenly and passes quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一阵刺痛」，来得突然、去得也快。

entries.definition: A sudden sharp feeling, often of hunger, guilt or sadness.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一阵剧痛或强烈的情绪」，常指饥饿、内疚或悲伤。

entries.definition: A strong regular beating pain, felt in rhythm with the pulse.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「搏动性的疼痛」，随脉搏一下一下地跳。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English word and the sound change that produced the modern spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语词，以及产生现代拼写的音变故事。

normal.en: Old English acan is the verb behind ache.
normal.cn: 古英语 acan 就是 ache 背后的动词。

normal.en: *aeg- is the reconstructed root for pain and sickness.
normal.cn: *aeg- 是重构出来的「疼痛、疾病」词根。

normal.en: The spelling ache was reshaped after Greek akhos, but the sound did not change.
normal.cn: 拼写 ache 参照希腊语 akhos 改写，但读音并没有改变。

normal.en: ache for and ache to do move the pain into longing.
normal.cn: 「ache for」与「ache to do」把疼痛转化为渴望。

normal.en: headache and toothache show the word inside compounds.
normal.cn: headache 与 toothache 展示了这个词在复合词中的位置。

abstract.en: Picture a thin thread tied to one spot inside the knee, pulled slowly all day.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细线系在膝盖内部某处，整天被缓慢地拉着。

abstract.en: The same thread can be tied to the chest when the pain is grief.
abstract.cn: 当痛来自悲伤时，同一根细线就被系到了胸口。

abstract.en: When the hand stops pulling, the thread may still be tight: that is the lingering ache.
abstract.cn: 拉线的手停下后，细线可能仍然绷着：这就是余痛。

examples.en: Her joints ached after the long walk.
examples.cn: 长途步行之后她的关节隐隐作痛。

examples.en: He had a dull ache in his lower back.
examples.cn: 他的下背部有一阵钝痛。

examples.en: She ached for news of her missing brother.
examples.cn: 她渴望得到失踪弟弟的消息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶克」——阴天里膝盖轻轻一声「诶」，那是钝钝的痛

root: 古英语 acan「疼痛」与名词 æce，属印欧词根 *aeg-「疼痛、疾病」；拉丁语 aeger「病弱的」只能算远亲，是否直接同源仍有争议，故不列为直接同族。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of ache follow one steady pull: a dull bodily pain, its location, its emotional form, its turn into longing, its old transitive use, the soreness of effort, its life inside compounds, and its lingering after the cause is gone.
sensesIntro.cn: ache 的八个义项都围绕同一种持续的拉扯：身体钝痛、痛的部位、心里的痛、转为渴望、旧的及物用法、运动后的酸痛、复合词中的痛，以及原因消失后的余痛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin thread is pulled steadily inside the body, never sharply and never quite stopping.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细线在身体内部被持续拉扯，既不尖锐，也始终不停。

branches.en: THE BODY: the dull pull is felt in general, then located in one part.
branches.cn: 身体线：闷闷的拉扯先被笼统感到，随后定位到某一部位。

branches.en: THE HEART: grief borrows the same dull pull and becomes heartache.
branches.cn: 心线：悲伤借用同一种闷痛，成为心痛。

branches.en: LONGING: an unending desire is a pull that will not let go.
branches.cn: 渴望线：无休止的愿望就是一条不肯松开的拉扯。

branches.en: THE WORD AT WORK: the old transitive use and the compounds fix the pain to a cause or a place.
branches.cn: 用词线：旧的及物用法与复合词把疼痛固定到某个原因或部位上。

branches.en: THE AFTERMATH: effort leaves soreness, and the pull can outlast its cause.
branches.cn: 余波线：用力留下酸痛，而拉扯可以比原因持续得更久。

intro.en: Ache is an Old English root with English compound forms; this section lists the root, the spelling story and the compounds.
intro.cn: ache 是古英语词根，并带有一批英语复合形式；这一部分列出词根、拼写故事与复合词。

latinIntro.en: No direct Latin descendant of the English word is recorded. Latin aeger 'sick' may be a distant relative through the same Indo-European root, but this is uncertain, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有记录到与这个英语词直接同源的拉丁词。拉丁语 aeger「病弱的」也许通过同一印欧词根与它远亲，但这并不确定，因此拉丁同族一栏留空。

items.example: The root is reconstructed, not directly attested.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根属于重构形式，并非直接见于文献。

items.example: The verb is recorded in Old English.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词在古英语中有记录。

items.example: The noun is the early form of ache.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是 ache 的早期形式。

items.example: The modern word covers both noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 现代英语中这个词兼作名词与动词。
它构成 aching。
它构成 headache。
它构成 toothache。
它构成 backache。

definition_zh: 实现；达到；取得；完成
definition_en: to succeed in reaching a goal, producing a result or completing a task through effort and persistence
core_image: 一步一步爬上山脊，抬头时界碑已经在脚下
scene: 山道陡峭，队员们在雨中互相拉扶。After six hours of climbing, the team finally achieved the summit.
sceneCN: 这里 achieve 是「到达、登上」（第 2 个义项：达到某个目标或地点）；句意为攀登六小时后，队伍终于登顶。

pos.zh: 动词：实现；达到；取得；完成

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「成就；达成」
由本词加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「可实现的；可达到的」
由本词加施动后缀 -er 构成，义为「成功者；有成就的人」
由本词加前缀 under- 构成，义为「表现不佳；未发挥潜力」
由本词加前缀 over- 构成，义为「超额完成；表现超出预期」

senses.title: To complete a task
senses.definition: to finish a task or piece of work that one has undertaken
senses.definitionCN: 完成自己承担的一项任务或一件工作
senses.example: The team achieved the repair before nightfall.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍在入夜前完成了修理。
senses.why: The core image is reaching the head of a climb: the task has been brought all the way to its end.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是爬到顶端：任务被一路推到它的终点。

senses.title: To reach a goal or place
senses.definition: to arrive at a goal, level or destination after effort
senses.definitionCN: 经过努力抵达某个目标、层次或目的地
senses.example: They achieved the summit just before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在暴风雨来临前登上了山顶。
senses.why: A chief means to the head or top; achieving is arriving at that top point.
senses.whyCN: a chief 意为「到头、到顶」；achieve 就是抵达那个顶点。

senses.title: To gain success
senses.definition: to produce a successful result, especially one that others notice
senses.definitionCN: 取得成功的结果，尤指他人能注意到的成果
senses.example: The young singer achieved success in her first season.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻歌手在第一个演出季就取得了成功。
senses.why: Reaching the top is visible from below, so success is the climb seen by others.
senses.whyCN: 登顶从下面看得见，因此成功是被别人看见的那次攀登。

senses.title: To win recognition
senses.definition: to gain respect, fame or approval through what one has done
senses.definitionCN: 因所做的事而获得尊重、名声或认可
senses.example: He achieved recognition as a translator of poetry.
senses.exampleCN: 他作为诗歌译者赢得了认可。
senses.why: The summit carries a name stone; recognition is the name written at the top.
senses.whyCN: 山顶立着刻名的界碑；声誉就是刻在顶端那个名字。

senses.title: To manage something very difficult
senses.definition: to succeed in doing something that seemed too difficult to do
senses.definitionCN: 成功做到某件看似难以完成的事
senses.example: The doctors achieved what the earlier team had thought impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 医生们做到了先前团队认为不可能的事。
senses.why: The higher the head, the harder the climb; achieving marks the climb that looked impossible.
senses.whyCN: 顶越高，攀登越难；achieve 标记的正是那次看似不可能的攀登。

senses.title: To reach a level or standard
senses.definition: to reach a required level or standard of quality or performance
senses.definitionCN: 达到要求的质量或表现水平与标准
senses.example: The factory achieved the safety standard after two audits.
senses.exampleCN: 经过两次审核，工厂达到了安全标准。
senses.why: A standard is a marked height; achieving means the line has been reached.
senses.whyCN: 标准就是一条标好的高度线；achieve 意味着已经够到那条线。

senses.title: To fulfil a promise
senses.definition: to carry out a promise or expectation completely
senses.definitionCN: 完整地履行承诺或满足期望
senses.example: The government achieved its promise of clean water for the village.
senses.exampleCN: 政府兑现了为村庄提供清洁用水的承诺。
senses.why: A promise is a point one has set ahead; fulfilling it is arriving there.
senses.whyCN: 承诺是事先设定的一个点；实现它就是抵达那里。

senses.title: To bring something to an end in older usage
senses.definition: in older usage, to bring something to completion or to finish it
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的用法，指把某事做到完结或结束它
senses.example: The old chronicle says he achieved the building in one year.
senses.exampleCN: 那部旧编年史说他一年就建成了这座建筑。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply finishing, because finishing is reaching the head of the work.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是「做完」，因为做完就是抵达这项工作的顶端。

intro.en: Achieve comes from a French phrase meaning to the head or top, and the whole family grows from that image.
intro.cn: achieve 来自一个意为「到头、到顶」的法语短语，整个词族都从这个意象生长出来。

items.en: caput meant 'head'; the phrase ad caput meant 'at the head, at the top'.
items.cn: caput 意为「头」；短语 ad caput 意为「在头部、在顶端」。

items.en: Old French chief meant 'head, top', and the phrase a chief meant 'to the head, at the top'.
items.cn: 古法语 chief 意为「头、顶端」，短语 a chief 意为「到头、到顶」。

items.en: The phrase a chief produced the verb achever, 'to bring to a head, finish, accomplish'.
items.cn: 短语 a chief 产生了动词 achever，义为「做到头、完成、实现」。

items.en: English borrowed the verb as acheven in the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪以 acheven 的形式借入这个动词；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The spelling settled as achieve, and the sense narrowed from finishing toward succeeding in reaching.
items.cn: 拼写最终固定为 achieve，词义也从「做完」收窄为「成功达到」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and relatives from the same head root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of reaching or completing something.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「头」词根构成的形式与亲属词；近义组收表示「达到或完成」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for something successfully done, formed with -ment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成就」，由动词加 -ment 构成。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning able to be reached or done.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可实现的」，由动词加 -able 构成。

entries.definition: The noun for a person who succeeds, formed with -er.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成功者」，由动词加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: A noun or adjective meaning the head of a group, from the same Latin caput.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「首领、首要的」，与 achieve 同出拉丁语 caput「头」。

entries.definition: To reach a goal, level or age after effort, often in formal use.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「达到」，多用于正式语境，强调经过努力抵达。

entries.definition: To complete a task successfully, with the emphasis on finishing it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「完成」，强调把任务做完。

entries.definition: To carry out a promise, duty or expectation fully.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「履行、实现」，强调把承诺、责任或期望完整兑现。

entries.definition: To arrive at a place or level; it names the arrival rather than the effort.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「到达」，只说明抵达，不强调所作的努力。

entries.definition: To make a plan or dream come true in fact.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「实现」，侧重让计划或梦想在现实中成真。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real French phrase for reaching the top and the suffixes that build the family.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的法语「到顶」短语，以及构成词族的后缀。

normal.en: a chief meant to the head: achieve is to bring something to its head or top.
normal.cn: a chief 意为「到头」：achieve 就是把某件事推到它的顶端。

normal.en: caput is head, and chief comes from the same Latin word.
normal.cn: caput 是「头」，chief 来自同一个拉丁词。

normal.en: achievable simply adds -able to the verb.
normal.cn: achievable 只是在动词后加了 -able。

normal.en: achievement adds -ment and turns the act into a thing.
normal.cn: achievement 加 -ment，把动作变成一个可以命名的东西。

normal.en: achieve a goal and achieve success show the two commonest objects.
normal.cn: 「achieve a goal」与「achieve success」展示了两个最常见的宾语。

abstract.en: Picture a climber in fog who keeps moving until the summit stone appears at the feet.
abstract.cn: 想象雾中的登山者一直往前走，直到界碑出现在脚下。

abstract.en: The same stone can be a task finished, a standard met or a promise kept.
abstract.cn: 同一块界碑可以是完成的任务、达到的标准，或兑现的承诺。

abstract.en: Achieving is not the mountain moving down; it is the climber reaching the top.
abstract.cn: 实现并不是山往下走，而是攀登者到达了顶端。

examples.en: She achieved her goal after two years of study.
examples.cn: 经过两年的学习，她实现了目标。

examples.en: The company achieved record sales last quarter.
examples.cn: 公司上季度取得了创纪录的销售额。

examples.en: Nothing is achieved without steady effort.
examples.cn: 没有持续的努力，就什么都做不成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿奇夫」——阿奇一步一步爬上山顶，终于实现目标

root: 古法语 achever「完成」源自短语 a chief「到头、到顶」，chief 出自拉丁语 caput「头」；本义是「做到头」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of achieve all describe one climb to a top point: finishing a task, reaching a goal or place, gaining success, winning recognition, doing the impossible, meeting a standard, keeping a promise, and the older sense of simply finishing.
sensesIntro.cn: achieve 的八个义项都在描述同一次「爬到顶点」：完成任务、抵达目标或地点、取得成功、赢得认可、做到难事、达到标准、兑现承诺，以及较旧的「做完」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a climber keeps moving up until the summit stone is underfoot.
core.cn: 核心意象：攀登者不断向上，直到界碑就在脚下。

branches.en: THE TASK: finishing work is reaching the head of it, which is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 任务线：把工作做完就是抵达它的顶端，这也是最古老的义项。

branches.en: THE DESTINATION: the top can be a place or a level actually reached.
branches.cn: 终点线：顶端可以是真正抵达的地点或层次。

branches.en: SUCCESS: the arrival becomes a result that counts as success.
branches.cn: 成功线：这次抵达变成可算作成功的结果。

branches.en: THE OUTSIDE VIEW: recognition is the name at the summit, and a standard is the marked height.
branches.cn: 外部视角线：认可是山顶的名字，标准则是标好的高度线。

branches.en: DIFFICULTY AND PROMISE: the highest climbs are the hardest, and a promise is a point set ahead.
branches.cn: 难度与承诺线：顶峰最难的攀登，而承诺是事先设定的那个点。

intro.en: Achieve comes from a French phrase for reaching the head, and English suffixes built the rest of the family.
intro.cn: achieve 来自意为「到顶」的法语短语，英语再用后缀扩展出整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin caput and its derivatives are recorded, so the family rests on attested Latin words rather than on reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caput 及其派生词均有记录，因此这个词族建立在有文献可考的拉丁词上，而非重构。

items.example: It forms part of the phrase a chief.
items.exampleCN: 它是短语 a chief 的一部分。

items.example: The phrase a chief meant to the top.
items.exampleCN: 短语 a chief 意为「到顶端」。

definition_zh: 成就；成绩；达成；业绩
definition_en: something important that has been done successfully, or the act of reaching a goal through effort
core_image: 山顶的界碑上刻着名字，证明这条路真的走完了
scene: 毕业典礼那天，礼堂里挂满了横幅。Winning the national contest was her greatest achievement at school.
sceneCN: 这里 achievement 是「成就」（第 1 个义项：通过努力取得的重要成果）；句意为赢得全国比赛是她在学校最大的成就。

pos.zh: 名词：成就；成绩；达成；业绩

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀 -ment 得到的动词，义为「实现；达到」
由动词加 -able 构成，义为「可实现的；可达到的」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「成功者；有成就的人」
由本词加前缀 over- 构成，义为「超额完成；表现超出预期」

senses.title: A concrete accomplishment
senses.definition: something specific and important that someone has succeeded in doing
senses.definitionCN: 某人成功完成的一件具体而重要的事
senses.example: Winning the race was his greatest achievement that year.
senses.exampleCN: 赢得那场比赛是他那年最大的成就。
senses.why: The summit stone carries a name: an achievement is the named result of a climb.
senses.whyCN: 山顶的界碑刻着名字：成就就是一次攀登留下的署名结果。

senses.title: The act of reaching a goal
senses.definition: the process or act of successfully reaching an aim one has worked for
senses.definitionCN: 成功抵达自己努力追求的目标的过程或行为
senses.example: The achievement of her goal took three quiet years.
senses.exampleCN: 她目标的达成花了三年默默的努力。
senses.why: The word also names the climbing itself, not only the stone at the top.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也指攀登本身，而不只是山顶那块石头。

senses.title: Academic performance
senses.definition: a student's measured success in school or college work
senses.definitionCN: 学生在学校或大学学业中可衡量的成绩
senses.example: The school rewards both academic achievement and teamwork.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校既奖励学业成绩，也奖励团队合作。
senses.why: In school the top of the climb is a measured mark, so results become achievement.
senses.whyCN: 在学校里，攀登的顶端是一个可测量的分数，成绩因此成了 achievement。

senses.title: Workplace performance
senses.definition: a record of successful results in a job or career
senses.definitionCN: 在职业或事业中成功结果的记录
senses.example: Her achievement in sales impressed the whole branch.
senses.exampleCN: 她在销售上的业绩让整个分公司都刮目相看。
senses.why: Work measures the height reached, and the measured height is called an achievement.
senses.whyCN: 工作会衡量你达到的高度，而被衡量的高度就叫 achievement。

senses.title: A major breakthrough
senses.definition: an advance that changes what was previously possible in a field
senses.definitionCN: 改变某一领域此前可能范围的进展
senses.example: The vaccine was a scientific achievement of the first order.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疫苗是头等的科学突破。
senses.why: When the climb opens a new route, the arrival changes the map for everyone.
senses.whyCN: 当攀登开出一条新路线，这次抵达就会改变所有人的地图。

senses.title: Something praiseworthy
senses.definition: an act or result that deserves praise and respect
senses.definitionCN: 值得称赞与尊重的行为或结果
senses.example: Raising four children alone was an achievement in itself.
senses.exampleCN: 独自抚养四个孩子本身就是一件值得称赞的事。
senses.why: Not every top is marked by others, but a hard climb still deserves the name.
senses.whyCN: 并非每个顶点都由别人标记，但艰难的攀登仍然配得上这个名称。

senses.title: A performance record
senses.definition: an official record of results achieved, used in evaluation
senses.definitionCN: 用于评估的、关于所取得成果的正式记录
senses.example: The annual report lists each department's achievements.
senses.exampleCN: 年度报告列出了各部门的绩效记录。
senses.why: The name at the summit is written down, and the written list becomes a record.
senses.whyCN: 山顶的名字会被记录下来，而记录下来的清单就成了档案。

senses.title: The realization of a collective aim
senses.definition: the successful realization of a long-term or shared aim, as in the achievement of independence
senses.definitionCN: 长期或共同目标的成功实现，如「独立的实现」
senses.example: The achievement of independence changed the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 独立的实现改变了整个地区。
senses.why: A whole people can climb one mountain, and the arrival belongs to all of them.
senses.whyCN: 一整个民族可以攀登同一座山，而这次抵达属于所有人。

intro.en: Achievement is the noun built on achieve, and it inherits the image of reaching the head or top.
intro.cn: achievement 是在 achieve 基础上构成的名词，继承了「到头、到顶」的意象。

items.en: The verb achever meant 'to bring to a head, finish', from the phrase a chief, 'to the top'.
items.cn: 动词 achever 意为「做到头、完成」，来自短语 a chief「到顶端」。

items.en: caput, 'head', is the deep source of chief and therefore of achieve and achievement.
items.cn: caput「头」是 chief 的深层来源，因此也是 achieve 与 achievement 的源头。

items.en: The verb appears as acheven in the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词在十四世纪以 acheven 的形式出现；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The noun with -ment is recorded later; the precise date of its first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 带 -ment 的名词记录得更晚；其首次使用的确切年代不确定。

items.en: School and workplace phrases such as academic achievement and lifetime achievement became standard.
items.cn: academic achievement、lifetime achievement 等学校与职场短语成为固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the verb and the derived forms of the same family; the near-meaning group gathers words for results that count.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词族的动词与派生形式；近义组收表示「值得算数的成果」的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to reach a goal or finish a task.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「实现、达到」，是本词的基础动词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning able to be reached or done.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可实现的」，由动词加 -able 构成。

entries.definition: The noun for a person who succeeds in reaching goals.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成功者」，由动词加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: The noun for performance below the expected level.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「表现不佳」，由本词加前缀 under- 构成。

entries.definition: The noun for performance beyond the expected level.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「超额完成」，由本词加前缀 over- 构成。

entries.definition: A completed task or skill, with the emphasis on finishing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成就、才艺」，侧重「完成」。

entries.definition: An impressive act that requires skill or courage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「壮举」，指需要技巧或勇气、令人印象深刻的行为。

entries.definition: The achieving of a desired aim, or the state of having done so.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成功」，指达成愿望或处于达成后的状态。

entries.definition: A formal noun for reaching a level or gaining a skill.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，名词，义为「达到、造诣」，指达到某水平或获得技能。

entries.definition: An important point in a process, like a stone marking distance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「里程碑」，指过程中的重要节点，本义是标距的石块。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real suffix and the fixed phrases the noun actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的后缀，以及这个名词实际出现的固定短语。

normal.en: achieve plus -ment turns the act into a result you can name.
normal.cn: achieve 加 -ment，把动作变成可以命名的结果。

normal.en: academic achievement is the standard phrase for school results.
normal.cn: 「academic achievement」是学业成绩的标准说法。

normal.en: a sense of achievement is the inner reward, not the prize.
normal.cn: 「a sense of achievement」是内在的回报，而不是奖品。

normal.en: lifetime achievement honours a whole career.
normal.cn: 「lifetime achievement」表彰的是整个职业生涯。

normal.en: the achievement of independence names a collective aim reached.
normal.cn: 「the achievement of independence」命名的是一个共同目标的达成。

abstract.en: Picture a summit stone with a name carved on it: that name is the achievement.
abstract.cn: 想象一块刻着名字的山顶界碑：那个名字就是 achievement。

abstract.en: The stone can be small or huge, personal or shared, but it always marks a height reached.
abstract.cn: 界碑可小可大，可属于个人也可属于众人，但它总标记着一个达到的高度。

abstract.en: Others may read the name, or no one may; the climb still happened.
abstract.cn: 别人可能读到这个名字，也可能无人知晓；但那次攀登确实发生过。

examples.en: Landing the contract was a major achievement for the young firm.
examples.cn: 拿下这份合同对这家年轻公司来说是一项重大成就。

examples.en: She listed her achievements in the application.
examples.cn: 她在申请材料中列出了自己的成就。

examples.en: The achievement of peace took years of patient talks.
examples.cn: 和平的实现花了多年耐心的谈判。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of achievement all name a height that was reached: a concrete result, the act of reaching, school and work records, a breakthrough, a praiseworthy act, a written record, and the realization of a shared aim.
sensesIntro.cn: achievement 的八个义项都在命名一个已经达到的高度：具体成果、达成的过程、学业与职业记录、重大突破、值得称赞的行为、书面档案，以及共同目标的实现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a named stone stands at the top of a climbed path.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段攀登路径的顶端立着一块刻名的界碑。

branches.en: THE STONE: a concrete accomplishment is the named result of one climb.
branches.cn: 界碑线：具体的成就就是一次攀登留下的署名结果。

branches.en: THE CLIMB: the word also names the act of reaching, whether the aim is personal or shared.
branches.cn: 攀登线：这个词也指抵达的动作本身，无论目标是个人还是共同。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: school, work and official records measure the height reached.
branches.cn: 衡量线：学业、职业与正式记录都在衡量所达到的高度。

branches.en: THE NEW ROUTE: a breakthrough opens a path that was not there before.
branches.cn: 新路线线：突破开出一条此前不存在的路径。

branches.en: THE QUIET TOP: some climbs deserve praise even when nobody marks them.
branches.cn: 无声顶端线：有些攀登即使无人标记，也值得称赞。

definition_zh: 酸；酸性物质；酸味的；尖刻的
definition_en: a chemical substance that releases hydrogen ions in water, or having a sour taste and a sharp, biting quality
core_image: 柠檬汁滴在舌尖，眉头一皱，酸得发紧
scene: 实验室的台面上摆着一排贴着标签的玻璃瓶。The litmus paper turned red when the acid was added to the beaker.
sceneCN: 这里 acid 是「酸」（第 1 个义项：能与碱反应、使指示剂变色的化学酸）；句意为把酸加入烧杯时，石蕊试纸变红了。

pos.zh: 名词：酸；酸性物质
形容词：酸的；酸性的；尖刻的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「酸性的；尖酸的」
由本词加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「酸度；酸性」
由本词加动词后缀 -ify 构成，义为「使酸化；变酸」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「尖刻地」

senses.title: A chemical acid
senses.definition: a substance that reacts with a base and turns blue litmus paper red
senses.definitionCN: 能与碱反应、使蓝色石蕊试纸变红的物质
senses.example: Hydrochloric acid is used to clean metal surfaces.
senses.exampleCN: 盐酸被用来清洗金属表面。
senses.why: The core image is the sour sting on the tongue: chemistry kept that sting and gave it a precise definition.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是舌尖上的酸刺感：化学保留了这种刺感，并给了它精确的定义。

senses.title: A sour taste
senses.definition: the sharp sour flavour of something such as lemon or vinegar
senses.definitionCN: 柠檬或醋之类东西那种尖锐的酸味
senses.example: The sauce has a pleasant acid taste.
senses.exampleCN: 这种酱料有一种宜人的酸味。
senses.why: The tongue tightens at the first drop, which is the original bodily reaction behind the word.
senses.whyCN: 第一滴入口，舌头就收紧，这正是这个词背后最初的身体反应。

senses.title: An acidic agent in everyday use
senses.definition: a specific acidic liquid or agent used in daily life, such as battery acid or stomach acid
senses.definitionCN: 日常生活中使用的某种酸性液体或物质，如电瓶酸或胃酸
senses.example: Stomach acid breaks down food after a meal.
senses.exampleCN: 饭后胃酸会分解食物。
senses.why: The sour sting is put to work: the same biting liquid now dissolves food or charges a battery.
senses.whyCN: 这种酸刺感被派上了用场：同一种带刺的液体如今分解食物或为电瓶充电。

senses.title: Biting, sharp speech
senses.definition: a remark full of sharp criticism or bitterness
senses.definitionCN: 充满尖锐批评或苦涩意味的话语
senses.example: His acid remarks made the room go quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 他尖刻的话让全场安静下来。
senses.why: The sour taste is borrowed for speech: words can sting the ear as juice stings the tongue.
senses.whyCN: 酸味被借来形容言语：话可以刺耳，正如汁液可以刺舌。

senses.title: Soil with a low pH
senses.definition: adjective describing soil that is below neutral in pH and suits certain plants
senses.definitionCN: 形容词，描述酸碱度低于中性、适合某些植物生长的土壤
senses.example: Rhododendrons grow well in acid soil.
senses.exampleCN: 杜鹃花在酸性土壤中长得好。
senses.why: A soil that tastes sour to the test is literally acid, so the taste word becomes a soil label.
senses.whyCN: 检验时呈酸味的土壤就是酸性的，于是味觉词变成了土壤标签。

senses.title: Rain made acidic by pollution
senses.definition: rainfall made acidic by dissolved pollutants such as sulphur dioxide
senses.definitionCN: 因溶解二氧化硫等污染物而变酸的降雨
senses.example: Acid rain damaged the forests downwind of the factory.
senses.exampleCN: 酸雨损害了工厂下风向的森林。
senses.why: The sour agent is now carried by the sky and falls onto the land.
senses.whyCN: 这种酸性物质如今被天空携带，落到大地上。

senses.title: A decisive test
senses.definition: a test that proves whether something is genuinely good or true
senses.definitionCN: 用来证明某事是否真正优良或真实的检验
senses.example: The final exam is the acid test of the whole course.
senses.exampleCN: 期末考试是对整门课程的决定性检验。
senses.why: Acid dissolves what is weak, so the acid test shows what survives.
senses.whyCN: 酸会腐蚀脆弱之物，因此酸测试显示的是什么能留下来。

senses.title: Slang for LSD
senses.definition: in informal use, a slang name for the drug LSD
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法中，对致幻剂 LSD 的俚语称呼
senses.example: The old song mentions acid and the summer of that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那首老歌提到「酸」和那年的夏天。
senses.why: A slang community borrowed the sharp word for a sharp experience, with no chemical link to the acid class.
senses.whyCN: 某个俚语圈子借用了这个尖利的词来形容一种强烈体验，与化学上的酸类并无关系。

intro.en: Acid goes back to a Latin word for being sour, and the same root also gave sharp and acrid.
intro.cn: acid 可上溯到拉丁语中表示「变酸」的词，同一词根还给出了 sharp 与 acrid。

items.en: *ak- 'sharp, pointed' is generally reconstructed; the deeper origin of the root is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *ak- 表示「尖锐的、锋利的」；这一词根更早的来源不确定。

items.en: acere meant 'to be sour, be sharp', and the adjective acidus meant 'sour, sharp'.
items.cn: acere 意为「发酸、尖锐」，形容词 acidus 意为「酸的、尖锐的」。

items.en: acidus described a sour taste and later a sharp manner; acidum as a noun is recorded in medieval chemistry.
items.cn: acidus 描述酸味，后来也描述尖刻的态度；名词 acidum 在中世纪的化学文献中有记录。

items.en: Old French acide passed the adjective into English; the exact date of borrowing is uncertain.
items.cn: 古法语 acide 把这个形容词带入英语；确切的借入年代不确定。

items.en: Chemistry fixed acid as a class of substances in the seventeenth century, and figurative uses such as acid test followed.
items.cn: 化学在十七世纪把 acid 固定为一类物质，随后又出现了 acid test 之类的比喻用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same sharp root; the near-meaning group gathers words for sour and biting qualities.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「尖锐」词根构成的词；近义组收表示「酸、尖刻」性质的词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning having the properties of an acid.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「酸性的」，由本词加 -ic 构成。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality or level of being acid.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「酸度、酸性」，由本词加 -ity 构成。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to make or become acid.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使酸化、变酸」，由本词加 -ify 构成。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning bitter and pungent in smell or taste, from the same sharp root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「刺鼻的、辛辣的」，与 acid 同出「尖锐」词根。

entries.definition: Adjective for the taste of lemon or vinegar, the everyday word behind acid.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「酸的」，指柠檬或醋的味道，是 acid 的日常对应词。

entries.definition: Adjective for a pleasantly sharp sour taste.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「酸得爽口的」，指宜人的尖酸味。

entries.definition: Adjective meaning keen and cutting, used of taste, smell and speech.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「尖锐的」，可用于味道、气味和言语。

entries.definition: Adjective for a harsh taste that is not sour but still unpleasant.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「苦的」，指一种并非酸味、但同样令人不适的强烈味道。

entries.definition: Adjective meaning able to burn or corrode, and also bitterly sarcastic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「腐蚀性的」，也可指「刻薄的、讽刺的」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real sharp root and the technical phrases acid actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的「尖锐」词根，以及 acid 实际出现的专门短语。

normal.en: *ak- is sharp: acid is the taste that cuts the tongue.
normal.cn: *ak- 是「尖锐」：acid 就是割在舌头上的那种味道。

normal.en: acidus is the Latin adjective for sour and sharp.
normal.cn: acidus 是拉丁语中表示「酸、尖」的形容词。

normal.en: acid test comes from the idea that acid dissolves what is weak.
normal.cn: 「acid test」来自「酸会腐蚀脆弱之物」这一想法。

normal.en: acid rain is pollution turned into a sour fall from the sky.
normal.cn: 「acid rain」是被污染变成的、从天空落下的酸。

normal.en: acidity adds -ity to name the measurable level.
normal.cn: acidity 加 -ity，命名的是可以测量的酸度。

abstract.en: Picture one drop of lemon juice on the tongue: the face tightens before any word arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴柠檬汁落在舌尖：话还没出口，脸先皱了起来。

abstract.en: The same drop can clean metal, charge a battery or dissolve stone, depending on strength.
abstract.cn: 同一滴液体按强度不同，可以清洗金属、为电瓶充电，或腐蚀石头。

abstract.en: A sharp word uses the same image without any liquid at all.
abstract.cn: 尖刻的话语没有任何液体，却用了同一个意象。

examples.en: Acid turns blue litmus paper red.
examples.cn: 酸会使蓝色石蕊试纸变红。

examples.en: The lemon has a sharp, acid taste.
examples.cn: 柠檬有一种尖锐的酸味。

examples.en: His acid remarks hurt more than the criticism itself.
examples.cn: 他尖刻的话比批评本身更伤人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿西德」——阿西舔了一口柠檬，酸得直皱眉

root: 拉丁语 acidus「酸的」来自 acere「变酸」，更早的词根 ac-「尖锐」，与 acrid、acute 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of acid all carry one sharp sting: the chemical class, the sour taste, the everyday agent, biting speech, acid soil, acid rain, the acid test, and the slang name for LSD.
sensesIntro.cn: acid 的八个义项都带着同一种尖锐的刺感：化学酸类、酸味、日常酸性物质、尖刻言语、酸性土壤、酸雨、酸测试，以及 LSD 的俚语称呼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of lemon juice lands on the tongue and the whole face tightens.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴柠檬汁落在舌尖，整张脸都皱紧了。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: chemistry names the class, daily life uses the agent, and the sky carries it down as acid rain.
branches.cn: 物质线：化学为这一类物质命名，日常生活使用这种物质，天空又以酸雨把它带回地面。

branches.en: THE TASTE AND THE FIELD: tongue and soil are both tested by the same sour sting.
branches.cn: 味觉与土地线：舌头与土壤都被同一种酸刺检验。

branches.en: THE TONGUE IN SPEECH: a sharp remark borrows the sting of sour juice.
branches.cn: 言语之舌线：尖刻的话借用了酸汁的刺感。

branches.en: THE PROOF: acid dissolves the weak, so the acid test shows what survives.
branches.cn: 检验线：酸腐蚀脆弱之物，因此酸测试显出什么能留存。

branches.en: THE SLANG EDGE: a subculture borrowed the sharp word for a strong experience, with no chemical link.
branches.cn: 俚语边缘线：某个亚文化借用了这个尖利的词来形容强烈体验，与化学并无关联。

intro.en: Acid is a Latin root with English suffixes; the same sharp root also built acrid and acute.
intro.cn: acid 是一个拉丁词根加英语后缀构成的词；同一「尖锐」词根还构成了 acrid 与 acute。

latinIntro.en: Latin acidus, acere, acetum and acies are all recorded, so the family rests on attested words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 acidus、acere、acetum 与 acies 均有记录，因此这个词族建立在有文献可考的词语上。

definition_zh: 承认；确认收到；感谢；致意
definition_en: to admit that something is true, confirm that something has been received, or show that someone or something is noticed and valued
core_image: 收信后在回执上郑重签下名字，表示「我收到了、我认了」
scene: 深夜的办公室里，桌上摊着一封道歉信。The manager refused to acknowledge that the decision had been wrong.
sceneCN: 这里 acknowledge 是「承认」（第 2 个义项：承认错误或失败）；句意为经理拒绝承认那个决定是错的。

pos.zh: 动词：承认；确认收到；感谢；致意

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「承认；致谢；回执」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「公认的」
由 acknowledged 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「未获承认的」

senses.title: To admit a fact
senses.definition: to accept that something is true, especially when it is unwelcome
senses.definitionCN: 接受某事为真，尤指接受不受欢迎的事实时
senses.example: The report acknowledges that the data are incomplete.
senses.exampleCN: 报告承认数据并不完整。
senses.why: The core image is signing a receipt: the signature says the fact has been received and accepted.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是在回执上签字：签下名字就意味着事实已被接收并接受。

senses.title: To admit a mistake or defeat
senses.definition: to admit that one has done something wrong or has lost
senses.definitionCN: 承认自己做错了事或已经失败
senses.example: He finally acknowledged that he had lost the argument.
senses.exampleCN: 他最终承认自己在争论中输了。
senses.why: The signature is hardest when the news is bad, yet that is exactly when it counts.
senses.whyCN: 消息越糟，落笔越难，但恰恰在这种时候，签名才算数。

senses.title: To confirm receipt
senses.definition: to confirm that a letter, message or delivery has arrived
senses.definitionCN: 确认信件、消息或货物已经送达
senses.example: Please acknowledge receipt of this email within two days.
senses.exampleCN: 请在两天内确认收到这封邮件。
senses.why: This is the core image in its plainest form: a receipt returns with a name on it.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心意象最朴素的形式：一张回执带着签名返回来。

senses.title: To express thanks for help
senses.definition: to say publicly that help or a contribution is valued
senses.definitionCN: 公开表示某人的帮助或贡献受到重视
senses.example: The author acknowledged the help of her students.
senses.exampleCN: 作者感谢了学生们的帮助。
senses.why: Acknowledging someone in print is like signing a receipt that says the debt of thanks is recorded.
senses.whyCN: 在书面上致谢，就像签下一张回执，表明这份人情已被记下。

senses.title: To greet with a nod
senses.definition: to show that one has seen someone by a nod, a smile or a brief greeting
senses.definitionCN: 通过点头、微笑或简短问候表示自己看见了某人
senses.example: She acknowledged the guard with a small nod.
senses.exampleCN: 她微微点头向门卫致意。
senses.why: A nod is a wordless signature: the other person is registered as seen.
senses.whyCN: 点头是一种无字的签名：对方被登记为「已看见」。

senses.title: To recognize someone's authority
senses.titleCN: 承认某人的地位或权威
senses.definition: to accept that someone has a right to be respected or obeyed
senses.definitionCN: 接受某人有权受到尊重或被服从
senses.example: The rebels refused to acknowledge the new king.
senses.exampleCN: 叛军拒绝承认这位新国王。
senses.why: Signing for a person's authority is a public act, like stamping a document.
senses.whyCN: 承认某人的权威是一种公开行为，就像给文件盖章。

senses.title: To recognize existence or validity
senses.definition: to accept that something exists or has legal or official validity
senses.definitionCN: 接受某物确实存在，或具有法律、官方效力
senses.example: The treaty acknowledges the rights of the islanders.
senses.exampleCN: 条约承认岛民的权利。
senses.why: A written record can make a claim official, just as a receipt proves a transaction.
senses.whyCN: 书面记录能让一项主张具有官方效力，正如回执能证明一笔交易。

senses.title: To admit a debt publicly
senses.definition: to admit publicly that one owes money or an obligation
senses.definitionCN: 公开承认自己欠有金钱或某种义务
senses.example: The company acknowledged a debt of ten thousand pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 公司承认了一万英镑的债务。
senses.why: The receipt becomes a promise in writing: the signature turns a debt into an admitted one.
senses.whyCN: 回执在这里变成书面承诺：签名把一笔债务变成已承认的债。

intro.en: Acknowledge grew from an Old English verb for knowing, and its spelling was later pulled toward know.
intro.cn: acknowledge 由古英语中表示「知道」的动词发展而来，拼写后来又被 know 拉近。

items.en: Old English cnāwan meant 'to know', and the prefixed form acnāwan meant 'to know, recognize'.
items.cn: 古英语 cnāwan 意为「知道」，带前缀的形式 acnāwan 意为「知道、认出」。

items.en: Middle English aknowen kept the sense 'to recognize, admit knowledge of'.
items.cn: 中古英语 aknowen 保留了「认出、承认知道」的义项。

items.en: The second element was reshaped under the influence of know, giving the modern spelling with -knowledge.
items.cn: 第二个成分受 know 的影响被改写，形成了带 -knowledge 的现代拼写。

items.en: The ending -ledge is a noun suffix of uncertain origin, perhaps related to the Old English suffix -lāc.
items.cn: 词尾 -ledge 是一个来源不确定的名词后缀，也许与古英语后缀 -lāc 有关。

items.en: From 'recognize' the word gained the senses of confirming receipt, thanking, and greeting.
items.cn: 从「认出」出发，这个词又发展出确认收到、致谢与致意的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and near-spellings of the same word; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of admitting or confirming.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个词的形式与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示「承认或确认」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for an act of admitting, thanking or confirming.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「承认、致谢、回执」，由本词加 -ment 构成。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning generally recognized or admitted.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「公认的」，由本词加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: The negated adjective meaning not admitted or not thanked.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「未获承认的」，由 acknowledged 加 un- 构成。

entries.definition: The noun for what is known; it looks close and helped reshape the spelling, but it is a different formation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「知识」，拼写相近并影响了本词的拼写，但构成方式不同。

entries.definition: To accept unwillingly that something is true, often against one's interest.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承认」，常指不情愿地接受某事为真。

entries.definition: To accept that something exists or is valid, or to identify someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承认、认出」，指接受某物存在或有效，或认出某人。

entries.definition: To admit a point after resistance, often in an argument.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「让步、承认」，指在争论中经过抵抗后承认某一点。

entries.definition: To admit something wrong or secret, often to an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「坦白、供认」，常指向权威承认错误或秘密。

entries.definition: To show or state that something is true or has arrived, close to the receipt sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「确认」，指证明或声明某事为真或已到达，接近「确认收到」的义项。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English verb for knowing and the fixed phrases of receipts and thanks.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语「知道」动词，以及回执与致谢的固定说法。

normal.en: cnāwan is to know, and acnāwan is to recognize.
normal.cn: cnāwan 是「知道」，acnāwan 是「认出」。

normal.en: know pulled the spelling toward knowledge, which is why the word looks longer than it sounds.
normal.cn: know 把拼写拉向 knowledge，所以这个词看起来比读音长。

normal.en: acknowledge receipt is the plainest case: a signature coming back.
normal.cn: 「acknowledge receipt」是最朴素的情形：一张带着签名的回执返回来。

normal.en: acknowledge a debt makes the signature into a written promise.
normal.cn: 「acknowledge a debt」把签名变成书面承诺。

normal.en: an acknowledged expert is someone whose name has been accepted by others.
normal.cn: 「an acknowledged expert」指的是名字已被他人接受的专家。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt form with one blank line: the signature is the moment knowledge becomes admission.
abstract.cn: 想象一张只留一行空白的回执：签名的瞬间，知道就变成了承认。

abstract.en: The same signature can mean I received it, I thank you, or I see you.
abstract.cn: 同一个签名可以表示「我收到了」「我谢谢你」，或「我看见你了」。

abstract.en: A nod across a room is the smallest possible version of that signature.
abstract.cn: 隔着房间的一次点头，就是这种签名最小的版本。

examples.en: She acknowledged that she had overlooked the error.
examples.cn: 她承认自己忽略了那个错误。

examples.en: Please acknowledge receipt of this letter.
examples.cn: 请确认收到这封信。

examples.en: His contribution was acknowledged at the ceremony.
examples.cn: 他的贡献在典礼上得到了感谢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克诺利奇」——阿诺在回执上签字：承认、确认收到

root: 中古英语 aknowen 源自古英语 acnāwan「知晓、认出」，第二成分受 know 影响改写；词尾 -ledge 来源不确定，一般认为与古英语后缀 -lāc 有关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of acknowledge all grow from a signature on a receipt: admitting a fact or a mistake, confirming receipt, thanking, greeting, recognizing authority, recognizing validity, and admitting a debt.
sensesIntro.cn: acknowledge 的八个义项都从回执上的签名生长出来：承认事实或错误、确认收到、致谢、致意、承认权威、承认效力，以及公开承认债务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a receipt comes back with a signature, meaning received, accepted and seen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张回执带着签名返回，意味着收到、接受与看见。

branches.en: THE RECORD: a fact or a right is written down and thereby accepted as true or valid.
branches.cn: 记录线：事实或权利被写下来，因而被承认为真实或有效。

branches.en: THE HARD SIGNATURE: mistakes and debts are the cases where signing costs the most.
branches.cn: 艰难签名线：错误与债务正是落笔代价最大的情形。

branches.en: THE RECEIPT: the plainest use, confirming that something has arrived.
branches.cn: 回执线：最朴素的用法，确认某物已经到达。

branches.en: THE DEBT OF THANKS AND AUTHORITY: thanking and recognizing power are both public acknowledgements.
branches.cn: 人情与权威线：致谢与承认权力都是公开的承认行为。

branches.en: THE NOD: the smallest signature, given without words.
branches.cn: 点头线：最小的签名，不用一个字。

intro.en: Acknowledge is an Old English knowing verb with a prefix, later reshaped by know and by the suffix -ledge.
intro.cn: acknowledge 是一个带前缀的古英语「知道」动词，后来受 know 与后缀 -ledge 影响而被改写。

latinIntro.en: The link to Latin goes through the Indo-European root for knowing, not through direct borrowing. Latin cognoscere and cognitus are distant relatives, and notus belongs to the same wider family.
latinIntro.cn: 它与拉丁语的关联是通过印欧语中表示「知道」的词根，而不是直接借入。拉丁语 cognoscere 与 cognitus 属于远亲，notus 同属更广的词族。
